key_insight: Biology-guided transcriptomic features provided more stable and useful immunotherapy response prediction than unstable gene-by-gene selection in advanced urothelial carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: Transcriptomic profiling may add the most value when used as a biologically informed layer on top of clinical and established biomarker data rather than as a standalone high-dimensional gene list.
method: Analyzed 298 IMvigor210 patients treated with atezolizumab.
Compared knowledge-guided tumor microenvironment gene-set features vs data-driven transcriptome-wide gene selection.
Benchmarked added predictive value beyond clinical variables and standard biomarkers using AUPRC.
evidence_signal: Knowledge-guided features improved AUPRC by 0.058 over clinical variables alone, while data-driven selection was unstable across folds (mean Jaccard 0.227) and underperformed the knowledge-guided approach by 0.150 in the clinical-plus-biomarker setting; external evaluation showed a similar pattern.
watch_item: Results come from a single trial cohort and the data-driven gene list was highly unstable, so broader validation is needed before implementation.
paper_title: Incremental Predictive Value and Representation of Transcriptomic Features for Immunotherapy Response in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
